newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slipped back with other bond markets during a fairly subdued session in which investors remained preoccupied by the likely impact of German and U.S. jobs figures due later in the week.

Traders said the contract tested support at 131.88 and then spent the rest of the day stuck in a fairly narrow range and that in the event of further declines, the contract would be well supported around 131.70.
There was some nervousness among primary dealers about the amount of potential demand for a new TEC 10 variable rate OAT the Treasury will sell for the first time on Thursday.

One trader said "people are already looking to Friday" when the February U.S. non-farm payrolls will be released. The key figures are likely to shape expectations for interest rate policy ahead of the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting on March 25.

Analysts said the German unemployment figures, due on Thursday, would be also be watched closely by investors gauging the extent of German economic weakness. A rebound in growth was seen as being important for helping Germany hit the Maastricth deficit criteria to join monetary union.

"We are looking for slightly better number, a bit of a bounce back from January," Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais, said. "It might help to stabilise the market, but if it's bad it will reignite concerns about delays" to monetary union.

Speculation about a delay to monetary union hit peripheral European bond markets and some traders said concern weighed slightly on the French market. They said investors were more nervous about the potential market reaction to rumours, rather than holding deep-rooted fears about a delay.

Lindsay said denials from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer that a delay was being considered certainly helped calm the market, especially as there was talk on Friday the German central bank had sparked the rumours in the first place.
"It helps, certainly, and it helps in the sense the market pays too much attention to what the Bundesbank has to say (about monetary union) in any case," Lindsay said.

Some traders said the main problem with the new TEC 10 was that domestic investors appeared reluctant to buy it on the grounds the yield curve still had further to flatten, an environment in which the floating rate bond suffers.
However, others said there was some interest from overseas investors in the 2009 TEC 10, principally as a useful bear market instrument.

The fact it would probably pay a slightly higher coupon, about 10 basis points, than the existing 2006 TEC was also seen as attractive, even though the longer-dated bond was more sensitive to yield curve flattening, analysts said.
As expected the Bank of France left its intervention rate unchanged at 3.10 percent at a regular money market tender on Monday. Call money also remained unchanged at 3-1/8 1/4 percent.
